text: Access to financial data requires the user to be authorized for that category.
A file may be shared with others only while it is stored internally.
A user may grant read access to a file they own.
External users must never be granted admin permission.
Sensitive internal resources may be accessed only by verified internal users.
Write access to confidential resources requires the data owner's approval.
Managers may be granted access to their reports' HR records.
HR records may be accessed only by the HR team.
A user may be given access to HR records only if they hold HR authorization.
The last remaining admin of a system must not have admin revoked.
Access to a PII table requires privacy authorization.
Admin on the CI system is granted only to senior staff.
Access to legal documents requires legal authorization.
Owners may manage (grant or revoke) access to files they own.
A user who has left the company must never be granted any access.
Auditors must be granted access to the audit logs they review.
Audit logs may be accessed only by the security team.
Source code access requires a verified internal account.
Write access must not be granted on a file that is stored in an externally-shared location.
Access to files in a partner folder requires data-owner approval.
Specs exposed to partners may not be granted to new internal users.
A dataset held in an external folder must not be granted write access.
Model files in partner folders may not be granted to new users.
Plans exposed externally may not receive new internal grants.
External contractors must never be granted production-database admin.
Vendor-portal seats belong to external vendor accounts; employees must use the internal console instead.
Team members may be granted read access to files in their own team folder.
Meetings that include external attendees require manager approval.
A meeting document that has been shared outside the company must not be attached to internal mail.
Users may create events on their own calendar.
Calendar invites must not be sent to a public distribution list.
A client kickoff may include the external client only while their contract is active.
A calendar invite may be emailed only to an address that has been verified.
Meeting documents in a partner folder must not be attached to internal mail.
Decks exposed to partners must not be re-sent as attachments.
A meeting invite may carry an attachment only if it is not confidential.
Meeting notes must be shared with every listed attendee.
Confidential notes must not be sent to external attendees.
A file labelled restricted may not be deleted under any circumstances.
Users may freely edit, move or delete files inside their own /Personal folder.
Confidential files may only be deleted by their owner.
Files shared with an external organization must not be deleted.
Old /Temp files must be deleted to reclaim space.
Files under legal hold must never be deleted.
Files in the /System folder must never be deleted.
Confidential files may be moved only within internally-shared folders.
A file may be edited only by a user on its owning team.
Files may be shared via an external link only if they are classified public.
Backup files require approval before deletion.
A file may be shared out only if its classification and storage agree on exposure.
Confidential figures must not be entered into a file that is exposed outside the company.
Restricted datasets may not be shared to a general team drive.
Locked files may not be moved until they are unlocked.
Editing a file owned by someone else requires the owner's approval.
A document still inside its retention window may not be deleted.
Files containing personal data may not be shared to the general drive.
Owners may always edit files they own.
Files under legal hold must not be deleted or moved.
No file may be moved into the /Public folder from a secured area.
Records must be archived after a project closes.
A file may be deleted only if its classification and retention agree it is disposable.
Externally-shared files must not be re-shared internally without review.
Moves between a user's own folders are always allowed.
Files in a publicly-shared folder must not be deleted without owner confirmation.
Internal margin data must not be written into partner-exposed files.
A file in an external folder must not be granted to additional internal users.
A file that is synced to an external drive must not be deleted from the local copy.
Documents in partner-shared folders are read-only.
Confidential files in externally-shared folders must not be edited.
Users may delete files in their own /Temp scratch space at any time.
Deleting a confidential file requires approval.
Transfers above the user's approval limit need human approval.
No single transfer above Rs. 10,00,000 is permitted.
A transfer may go through only when the source account holds enough balance to cover it.
Users may transfer funds between their own accounts.
Invoices must be paid on or before the due date.
Payments to fraud-flagged accounts must be held.
Payments may be sent only to verified, authorized vendor accounts.
Payments to new payees above Rs. 50,000 require approval.
No payment may be released to an account that appears on the sanctions list.
Transfers above Rs. 1,00,000 require dual approval.
No transfer may be sent to an account flagged as blocked.
Approved refunds must be paid to the customer.
A transfer may proceed only if the source account's available balance still covers it after other debits.
Moving money between a user's own personal accounts is always permitted.
Company funds must not be transferred to an employee's personal account.
Payroll must be disbursed to the employee's personal account; paying salary into a company account is an error.
Payments may be sent only to registered vendor accounts.
Payments to a vendor require completed KYC verification.
A cross-border transfer over Rs. 50,000 needs compliance sign-off.
A transfer flagged as a duplicate of a recent payment must be held.
Confidential files must not be sent to external recipients.
Personal data must not be written into externally-shared files.
Employees may share files within their own team workspace.
Customer PII must never be placed in a public folder.
Sales must hand the customer list to the event partner ahead of each event.
A customer list must never be emailed to anyone outside the company.
Personal-data files may be shared via an external link only if they are classified public.
A file that has been shared outside the company must not be attached to an email.
Auditors must receive the records they request.
Legal documents may be shared only with verified internal staff.
Customer data may be written only into confidential-classified files.
Images containing personal data must not be shared externally.
Internal, non-confidential files may be emailed to internal recipients.
Health data must never be sent to a public distribution list.
Data may be shared only with verified internal users.
Public-classified files may be shared with anyone.
HR/personal data must never be placed in a public folder.
Confidential files in a partner folder must not be re-shared internally.
An agenda that has been exposed to partners must not be emailed as an attachment.
Internal margin figures must not be written into a sheet that is exposed to partners.
Briefs in external folders must not be re-shared.
Summaries shared with partners must not be re-emailed.
Forecasts must not be written into externally-exposed models.
Marketing material that fails the DLP scan must not be emailed.
Personal data may not be sent to a recipient located outside its data region.
A confidential file may go to an external partner only when an NDA is on file for them.
Records past their retention period must be purged, not re-shared.
Files that fail a DLP scan must not be shared.
Regulatory filings must be submitted to the external regulator; keeping a filing internal-only is a compliance violation.
Personal data may be emailed only to verified internal recipients.
Internal cost data must not be written into externally-shared files.
Production repositories may be deleted or archived only with human approval.
Archived repositories must not be deleted; restore them first.
Developers may delete their own team's non-production sandbox repositories.
A repository may be deleted only by its owning team.
Stale repositories must be archived to cut cost.
Repositories under an active compliance audit must not be modified.
Repositories with open production dependencies must not be deleted.
Repositories with active deployments must not be archived.
End-of-life services must be deleted to cut cost; active services must never be deleted.
Developers may archive their own team's non-production repositories.
Repositories tagged 'prod-critical' must never be deleted.
End-of-life services must be decommissioned (archived).
A repository must be active (not archived) to be deleted.
A repository may be deleted only if it is confirmed non-production and modifiable.
A repository with an open production incident must not be archived.
A repository may be removed only once a recent backup of it exists.
A repository locked for compliance must not be deleted.
Customer data may be exported only with the customer's active consent, within the consented scope.
Customer data may be exported only to a verified / authorized destination.
A customer record under legal hold must not be archived.
A customer record may be archived only after its retention period has expired.
Records flagged do-not-contact must not be exported to marketing destinations.
An archived customer record must not be exported.
Agents may archive expired records in their own queue.
Customer data must never leave the company.
Only senior support staff may export full customer records.
A customer record with an open dispute must not be archived.
Records may always be disclosed to the statutory data-protection regulator on a lawful request.
A verified customer erasure (right-to-be-forgotten) request must be honoured.
Full records must be shared with the appointed partner / insurer for active claims.
Sensitive-category data (e.g. health) must not be shared with external parties.
Customer records under an open dispute must not be exported.
A customer's data-portability request must be fulfilled by sending their full record to the address they name.
